title: Safely Through Another Week
description: Safely Through Another Week in Tonic Solfa to RATISBON (WERNER), doh is D: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 5 verses and a piano.
about: John Newton wrote these words. They were printed in Olney Hymns (London, 1779), Book II, hymn 40, “Saturday evening”.

The book printed the words without tunes, marked Sevens, six lines (7.7.7.7.7.7), to be sung to any tune of that metre. This page sets them to RATISBON (WERNER); any other Sevens, six lines tune fits them as well.
underlay: Safe-ly through an-oth-er week, God has brought us on our way, Let us now a bless-ing seek On th'ap-proach-ing sab-bath day: Day, of all the week, the best; Em-blem of e-ter-nal rest!

lines: Safely through another week,
God has brought us on our way,
Let us now a blessing seek
On th' approaching sabbath-day:
Day, of all the week, the best;
Emblem of eternal rest!
Mercies, multiplied each hour,
Through the week our praise demand;
Guarded by almighty pow'r,
Fed and guided by his hand:
Though ungrateful we have been,
Only made returns of sin.
While we pray for pard'ning grace,
Through the dear Redeemer's name;
Show thy reconciled face,
Shine away our sin and shame:
From our worldly cares set free,
May we rest, this night, with thee.
When the morn shall bid us rise,
May we feel thy presence near;
May thy glory meet our eyes,
When we in thy house appear!
There afford us, Lord, a taste
Of our everlasting feast.
May thy gospel's joyful sound
Conquer sinners, comfort saints;
Make the fruits of grace abound,
Bring relief for all complaints:
Thus may all our Sabbaths prove
Till we join the church above!

source: John Newton and William Cowper, Olney Hymns (1779)
licence: Public domain: John Newton died in 1807.
credits: Words by John Newton (1725–1807), public domain, as printed in Olney Hymns (1779); set to RATISBON (WERNER) by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
